clue.text: Rhetorical description of artwork, as in 'peculiarly spheric'

indicators.note: something done peculiarly is done oddly, so the letters of the following word come out in a strange order
the clue asks for the short word to sit inside the scrambled word that follows

blocks.note: the word to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic quotes a phrase from a florid description of a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: ECPHRASIS is Chambers' spelling with C of the more familiar ekphrasis; the quotation marks dress the fodder up as a quoted example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecphrasis is the rhetorical figure of a vivid verbal description, especially of a painting or other work of visual art.

clue.text: My home is in Central America roughly? Some way south of it actually

definitions.text: My home is in Central America roughly? Some way south of it actually

indicators.note: the speaker's home is placed inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for the region
ca, short for circa, means roughly or approximately
the speaker of this clue lives in Rio de Janeiro

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a geography mistake: their home is not in Central America but far to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the answer: a native of Rio, whose city sits between the two CAs, though really thousands of miles south of Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carioca is a native or inhabitant of Rio de Janeiro, a city in Brazil, which lies well south of Central America.

clue.text: Bairn's spotty appearance, tucking into e.g. pasty?

definitions.note: adjective: Scots, as the bairn signals

indicators.note: something tucking into food goes inside it

blocks.note: a pasty is a kind of pie
someone's look is their appearance

explanation.surface: A child gets spots on its face from eating pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: A bairn is a Scottish child, so the definition asks for the Scots word for spotty; a pasty is a pastry turnover with a savoury filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Plookie is Scots for pimply, covered with plooks, the Scottish word for pimples or spots.

clue.text: Maori greeting has not finished before mum is half cut

indicators.note: a word not finished stops short of its final letter
cutting a two-letter word in half keeps only one of its letters

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
ere is an old word for before
ma is an informal word for mother
half of the two-letter word

explanation.surface: A welcome is cut short before mother, who has had a few drinks, can finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Half cut is British slang for tipsy, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Haere mai is the Maori phrase of welcome used in New Zealand, meaning come here or welcome.

clue.text: Disturbance after expulsion of US bum

indicators.note: after the named letters are expelled, the longer word is left without them

blocks.note: a rumpus is a noisy commotion
the two letters thrown out

explanation.surface: An American layabout causes trouble after being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum looks like the American word for a tramp, helped by US; here it is the British word for backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the buttocks or hindquarters, which British slang calls the bum.

clue.text: Whiskey drunk so has rum (8, two words)

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order and need to be put straight

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been drinking whiskey and is now on the rum as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour mash is American whiskey distilled from a mash started with some spent mash from an earlier batch, as in Tennessee and bourbon making.

clue.text: Shut in as of old, confined to grim barracks

indicators.note: letters confined to a phrase are held within it, crossing the gap between words

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Soldiers of long ago were locked up in bleak quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As of old' marks an archaic word, a variant of embar.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbar is an obsolete verb meaning to enclose or bar in, to shut someone up.

clue.text: Dead hind, grey

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
hind as an adjective means back, at the rear

explanation.surface: A female deer has died, its coat grey.
explanation.walkthrough: Hind looks like the female red deer; here it means back, the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic word for dreary or gloomy, and grey is used in the same sense of dull and cheerless.

clue.text: Advanced in age (but certainly not late)

indicators.note: the first item is placed inside the second

blocks.note: an eon is an age, an immeasurably long period
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An elderly person is said to be getting on but very much alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Late in the surface means dead; in the definition it means the opposite of early, and the answer belongs to the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoan means of or relating to dawn, the earliest part of the day, so it is the opposite of late.

clue.text: Playwright, nice when played with identical characteristics?

indicators.note: a word that is played with is toyed with, its letters moved around

blocks.note: J. M. Synge was the Irish playwright of The Playboy of the Western World
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatist turns out to be pleasant whenever his works are staged.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: genetically identical organisms share characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Syngeneic describes genetically identical individuals, such as identical twins, so their tissues can be transplanted without rejection.

clue.text: What may dry up in summer, feeding communal aqueducts

definitions.text: What may dry up in summer

indicators.note: something feeding into the phrase is sitting inside it, spread across the join of its two words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Shared water channels are fed by a stream that runs dry in hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: the watercourse is the thing that may dry up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nala (nullah) is an Indian watercourse or ravine that carries water in the rains and is often dry in the hot season.

clue.text: Old apple Brit long ago brought from the east?

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading from right to left, backwards

blocks.note: Pom is Australian slang for a Briton
of yore means in times long past

explanation.surface: An ancient variety of apple is said to have been introduced by a Briton returning from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomeroy is an old variety of English apple, now rarely grown.

clue.text: Rilke's introduction in one of his compositions?

indicators.note: the introduction to a name is its opening letter
the chosen letter is to be placed inside the following item

blocks.note: Rilke was a poet, so his compositions are poems
the poet's initial

explanation.surface: A literary scholar wonders whether the preface Rilke wrote was itself one of his poems.
explanation.walkthrough: Rilke's introduction does double duty: the initial R that goes into the poem, and a preface by the poet, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or preamble to a book or speech, an introductory piece of writing.

clue.text: Churchman who's with it is organized for most of Sunday, I bet

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it except its final letter
once letters are organized they have been arranged into a new order

blocks.note: the day without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric with modern ideas will, the speaker suspects, be running most of the Sunday services.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the churchman together with IT rearranges into SUNDA plus I BET, so take IT away from those nine letters and rearrange the rest into SUBDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdean is a cathedral clergyman ranking next below the dean and acting as deputy, so he is a churchman.

clue.text: Short composition, an opening for Scot coming into existence

indicators.note: the earlier items come into the word that follows, sitting inside it

blocks.note: esse is the philosophical term for existence or being
the indefinite article
yett is the Scots word for a gate

explanation.surface: A brief piece of writing opens the door for a Scot to begin his life.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayette is a little essay, a brief prose composition on one subject.

clue.text: Quite a stretch for shah, a prince in grip of pain

indicators.note: a thing held in the grip of another is clasped inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a ras is an Ethiopian prince or chief
a pang is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: A ruler of Persia complains of a painful stretch while a prince is in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite a stretch' is a distance, not a muscle strain, and the shah tells you it is Persian.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasang is an old Persian unit of distance of roughly three and a half miles, a long way for a shah to travel.

clue.text: Juridical district, given voice but lacking power

indicators.note: lacking something means doing without it, so it is taken out

blocks.note: something given voice has been uttered aloud in words
P is the physics symbol for power; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A legal district is allowed to speak but has no authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A soken was a district under a particular jurisdiction in Old English law, the area where a lord held a right of court.

clue.text: Lichen expert fed to deer

indicators.note: something fed to another goes inside it

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
a oner is an expert, someone unique at something

explanation.surface: A specialist in lichens is given to a deer as food.
explanation.walkthrough: Lichen expert reads as one phrase, a botanist; the definition is lichen alone and the expert goes in the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-rag is a common name for a crustose lichen that grows on rocks.

clue.text: It's great (possibly) near Llandudno making millions in e.g. tin

indicators.note: one letter is put inside the following item

blocks.note: tin is mined as an ore
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Something grand on the north Welsh coast earns millions from tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Orme is the limestone headland beside Llandudno, a resort in North Wales; 'great (possibly)' hints at that name while sounding like praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Orme is the name of the headlands at Llandudno, the larger of which is called the Great Orme.

clue.text: Ringlike circle: head of temple entering his inner chambers

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the letter entering goes inside the following word

blocks.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
cellae, plural of cella, are the inner sanctuaries of a classical temple
the first letter of the building

explanation.surface: A circular ring of priests: the high priest goes into the temple's inner rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: His refers back to temple: the inner chambers of a temple are its cellae.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocellate means marked with ocelli, eye-like spots with a ring of colour, so ringlike in pattern.

clue.text: Sign of wound? One marks it having penetrated (maybe)

definitions.text: Sign of wound? One marks it having penetrated (maybe)

indicators.note: pieces that have penetrated something have gone inside it

blocks.note: a healed wound leaves a scar
the Roman numeral for one
M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scar is evidence of a wound, and a blade that cut deep may have left it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the curved sword itself: a weapon that can leave a scar once it has gone in.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, the kind of blade that may leave a scar after slicing into someone.

clue.text: Brian maybe in bar, having retired one assumes?

definitions.note: a surname: the actor Brian Blessed is the example

indicators.note: the first item sits inside the next

blocks.note: someone who has retired for the night is presumably in bed
bar as a preposition means except, as less does

explanation.surface: Someone guesses Brian has given up work and now spends time in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Blessed is the booming-voiced English actor. Retired in the surface means stopped working; in the wordplay it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed is the surname of the actor Brian Blessed, so Brian is an example of a person named Blessed.

clue.text: Blind fool in v-very small time breaking leg

indicators.note: a word broken open has something inserted into the gap

blocks.note: taken as written
a small time is a minute, abbreviated MIN, and the stammered v-very makes its first letter stutter

explanation.surface: A sightless idiot breaks a leg in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in the clue is copied in the wordplay: as v-very repeats a letter, the minute's M is said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemming is a person who follows the crowd unthinkingly, after the rodents' supposed mass rush over cliffs.

clue.text: Char every other bit of veal in chaotic soirée (8, two words)

indicators.note: every other bit means taking the second and fourth letters, skipping those between
a chaotic jumble of letters has lost its order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the even-numbered letters of the meat
the party word, with its accent dropped

explanation.surface: At a disorderly evening party someone burns half the veal.
explanation.walkthrough: Char looks like a verb about scorching the veal; here it is the noun for tea, from Chinese cha. ROSIE LEE is Cockney rhyming slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both char and Rosie Lee are informal British words for tea, the drink.

clue.text: Such aerials are highly directional, locally spotted reversing electric current

indicators.note: reversing a word turns its letters to run back to front

blocks.note: gay is a northern dialect word meaning speckled or spotted
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A radio engineer notes that these directional aerials were seen nearby, sending current backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word, the convention Azed uses for regional senses in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yagi aerial, named after its Japanese inventor, is a beam antenna of parallel elements that picks up signals strongly from one direction.

clue.text: Member admitted to Indian region monastery (Buddhist)

indicators.note: someone admitted to a place is let inside it

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP is let into a Buddhist monastery in an Indian region.
explanation.definitionFit: A gompa is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery or temple, common in the Himalayan regions.

clue.text: For and against aid in freeing trapped miners

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
to can mean against, as in face to face or shoulder to the door

explanation.surface: Opinions differ on equipment to help rescue miners stuck underground.
explanation.walkthrough: For and against look like pros and cons of a debate; they are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Proto was a trademark self-contained breathing apparatus used by mine rescue teams to reach trapped miners.

clue.text: Part of dope (fragrant)? Features in crime Lewis recalled

indicators.note: something that features in a phrase appears inside it, here across a word boundary
recalled is read as called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words, before turning round

explanation.surface: A fragrant drug turns up in a crime solved by Inspector Lewis, the TV detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope here is not a drug but varnish or lacquer; the surface invites thoughts of cannabis in an Oxford crime drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin used in varnishes, lacquers and ointments, so it can be an ingredient of a varnish.

clue.text: Green nut cake for being distributed around middle of tea

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter
letters being distributed are spread about into a new arrangement
the rearranged letters go around the single central letter

blocks.note: the letters to be shuffled
the central letter of the drink

explanation.surface: An environmental enthusiast asks for cake to be handed round at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Green and nut both read as adjectives or food in the surface; together they mean an environmental fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-freak is an informal term for a fanatical environmentalist, someone obsessively green, a nut about ecology.

clue.text: Suggestion of Shakespearian scholars (hence a supposition in part)

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters within it

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word, a short word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Scholars of Shakespeare put forward a theory, so the clue calls it partly a supposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis looks like a comment on the definition, but it holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceas is a reading proposed by Shakespeare scholars, a conjectural form of cease, so the word itself is their suggestion.

clue.text: Cuckoo clock, English, faulty, reduced by two hundred

indicators.note: a faulty arrangement is out of order and must be fixed
something reduced by an amount has that amount taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
Roman numerals for two hundred, the letters removed

explanation.surface: An English cuckoo clock has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo clock reads as one object; cuckoo is the definition and the clock is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The koel is a large cuckoo of South Asia and Australasia, named after its call.

clue.text: In the time of these, he's abandoned, unruly 13

indicators.note: letters that are abandoned are left out of the word before them
unruly letters will not stay in order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the word whose letters are reduced
the letters taken out of the previous word
the answer to 13 across

explanation.surface: Back in their era, the clue says, someone was deserted by an unruly preface.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H, E and S from THESE leaves T and E, which join the letters of 13 across before shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempore is Latin for 'in the time of', used before a name or date to place something in a particular reign or period.

clue.text: It's useful for flower arrangers, wanting nothing unaltered

blocks.note: zero, nothing, is written as O
as is means left in its present state, unaltered

explanation.surface: A tool florists find handy needs no changes at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis is the trade name for the green foam blocks florists push stems into.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis floral foam is a water-absorbing block used by florists to hold stems in place in an arrangement.

clue.text: Denoting botanical cell layer, cheers part of flower

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
a petal is one segment of a flower's corolla

explanation.surface: A botanist toasts the cell layer found within a flower part.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapetal is the adjective from tapetum, the nourishing layer of cells lining the pollen sacs of an anther.

clue.text: Minister to chasten dean losing letters left and right

indicators.note: stripping letters from both ends leaves only a run from the inside of the phrase

blocks.note: the letters left once both ends are trimmed away

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told to discipline a dean who keeps dropping letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister looks like a noun for a clergyman, but with 'to' it is the verb, to care for.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to attend to their needs, which is what to tend means.

clue.text: Arctic vehicle, stratagem protecting wobbly legs (9, two words)

indicators.note: wobbly things are unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order
a thing protecting another wraps around it

blocks.note: a dodge is a cunning trick or ruse
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A polar transport is a clever trick that keeps unsteady legs safe on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog sledge is a sledge pulled by a team of dogs, the classic means of travel across Arctic snow.
